chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid from al-Fadl ibn Sahil from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the charity that was forbidden to them (the Banu Hashim), so he said: 'It is the obligatory alms-tax (Zakat), and the charity of one of us to another has not been forbidden upon us.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Zakat and Sadaqah regarding the Banu Hashim's prohibition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the distinction is drawn between the specific obligatory alms-tax (Zakat) prohibited for Banu Hashim and general voluntary charity (Sadaqah), which remains permissible. This clarification resolves potential confusion regarding their financial status, affirming that while they are excluded from the communal Zakat pool, they may still receive gifts and voluntary aid from others. This ruling underscores the nuanced application of Quranic verses regarding the recipients of Zakat within Shia jurisprudence.
